feature1.prompt: Inheritance-diagram 404 links with SVG: The current documentation generator produces SVG inheritance diagrams that lead to 404 errors when the diagram is created in a file located in a subdirectory. The bug occurs because the URL construction logic incorrectly treats the link as relative to the embedding file instead of the SVG file itself. This behavior contrasts with the default (PNG) mode, which works as expected. The expected behavior is that, regardless of the file’s location, the generated SVG diagram contains links that correctly point to the target HTML files in the proper subdirectory structure.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on modifying the URL construction logic in the HTML visitor for the inheritance diagram. In the file sphinx/ext/inheritance_diagram.py, adjust the conditions in the html_visit_inheritance_diagram function so that when the output format is SVG, the URL is constructed correctly. Ensure that the fix differentiates between internal and external references and that relative paths resolve relative to the SVG file’s location rather than the embedding document.
feature1.entrypoint: sphinx/ext/inheritance_diagram.py – specifically, the html_visit_inheritance_diagram function (around the code block starting at line 412) where the URL for SVG links is constructed. Developers should update the logic that currently prepends '../' to the refuri and refid so that it correctly reflects the file structure.

feature2.prompt: Inheritance-diagram 404 links with SVG: The issue arises when SVG inheritance diagrams are generated in non-root directories, resulting in links that do not correctly resolve and instead lead to 404 pages. The problem is caused by incorrect relative link construction, which does not account for the document’s nested location. Although the PNG mode does not show this problem, the SVG mode must generate links that accurately match the file organization so that each link points to its intended HTML document. The overall goal is to eliminate 404 errors by ensuring the links reflect the true location of the referenced pages.
feature2.hint_texts: Concentrate on updating the test suite to fully validate the new URL generation logic. This includes modifying existing test configurations and adding new test cases to simulate both root and nested directory scenarios. Ensure that scenarios with external (intersphinx) as well as internal links are covered so that the tests verify the correct path resolution and that links no longer produce 404 errors.
feature2.entrypoint: Test file modifications are required in several locations: update tests/roots/test-ext-inheritance_diagram/conf.py to include the necessary extensions, adjust tests/roots/test-ext-inheritance_diagram/index.rst and add tests/roots/test-ext-inheritance_diagram/subdir/index.rst along with related auxiliary files (such as tests/roots/test-ext-inheritance_diagram/subdir/other.py and tests/roots/test-ext-inheritance_diagram/test.py). Also, update tests/test_ext_inheritance_diagram.py to incorporate the proper handling of SVG links and intersphinx link mapping.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features work with the inheritance diagram extension and share the sphinx configuration and URL generation mechanism. The core HTML output generated by sphinx and the inheritance_diagram extension is a common resource for both the code fix and its validation.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature 1 implements the core fix by correcting the URL generation logic in the extension. Feature 2 ensures that this fix is properly validated by updating and extending the test suite. Integration is achieved by having the tests in Feature 2 exercise the changes made in Feature 1 across both root-level and nested directory scenarios.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature 1 need to clearly describe the new URL construction logic and any nuances in handling internal versus external links. Similarly, developers on Feature 2 must coordinate on the expected output of the diagrams to write comprehensive tests. Regular discussions are recommended to ensure the updated tests accurately reflect the behavior of the modified code.
